dataset.name: HD-EPIC
dataset.license_or_access_note: HD-EPIC official Bristol research distribution; original recording attribution retained. User confirmed dataset authorization.

observed_events.description: A dark broad-headed spatula stirs onions in a low, wide single-long-handle frying pan.
An oval wooden spoon stirs potatoes in the separate high-sided saucepan with a single long handle; the repeated later stirring shows the same relation.
The wearer takes a recipe tub; no active spoon-to-pan relation is shown. Both vessels and resting utensils are background reminders shared by both conditions.
The wearer turns toward prepared ingredients beside the cooker; no active spoon-to-pan relation is shown. The identical frame is shared across conditions.
At another counter, the wooden oval spoon scrapes food off a perforated potato masher over a plate. Neither cooking vessel is in view.

unsupported_claims: Exact cookware brand, capacity, diameter or material
Physical retail identity of the wooden spoon
A new independent camera wearer; this is a new recording from existing HD-EPIC participant P03

screening.real_user_need: Buy one spare matching the shape and handle arrangement of a pan used while cooking; the user refers to it through a later utensil action.
screening.scope_note: New recording; independent blind review pending. Near/far use the same fully specified instruction upfront.
screening.proposed_instruction: Next time I want to cook two batches at once. I would like a spare like one of the pans I cooked with here. Add one to my cart, matching its general shape and handle arrangement. Brand, colour, material and size can differ. One pan, not a multi-pan set; a lid is fine.

construct.research_question: Does the model recover the earlier cookware-to-utensil relation when the identifying later action is separated from that relation by more observed cooking events?
construct.belief_before: Both the shallow pan used with the broad dark spatula and the deep saucepan used with the oval wooden spoon are plausible cookware references.
construct.belief_after: The last action identifies the oval wooden spoon without showing cookware; earlier views identify its saucepan partner.
construct.required_behavior_change: Link the utensil in the final scraping action to its earlier cookware partner; add one matching pan.
construct.no_update_failure: Without the physical reference either cooking vessel is plausible; the experiment supplies this same reference upfront to both conditions.
construct.overupdate_failure: Buying both vessels or buying the utensil instead of cookware does not satisfy the one-pan request.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The binding views identify which utensil was used in which vessel. The final counter views identify the requested utensil but omit cookware. Neither fact set alone identifies the requested vessel.

task_blueprint.ambiguous_instruction: Next time I want to cook two batches at once. I would like a spare like one of the pans I cooked with here. Add one to my cart, matching its general shape and handle arrangement. Brand, colour, material and size can differ. One pan, not a multi-pan set; a lid is fine.
task_blueprint.oracle_instruction: Next time I want to cook two batches at once. I would like a spare like the pan I used with the utensil I use to scrape food off the masher at the end. Add one to my cart, matching its general shape and handle arrangement. Brand, colour, material and size can differ. One pan, not a multi-pan set; a lid is fine.
task_blueprint.canonical_question: Which of the pans you used do you mean?
task_blueprint.canonical_answer: The one I used with the utensil I use to scrape food off the masher at the end.
